labels.text: 60% of the volume of body fluids

depictions.what: body fluid drawn in two compartments: inside the cells (ICF) and outside the cells (ECF)
the ICF compartment drawn as 60% of all body fluid, so it is the larger of the two
the inside of a cell holding protein, water, electrolytes and solutes
the ECF split into types, each labeled: intravascular, interstitial and transcellular
intravascular fluid drawn inside a blood vessel as whole blood: red blood cells, white blood cells, plasma and platelets
interstitial fluid drawn outside the blood vessel, between the cells
transcellular fluid shown apart, named for its areas: cerebrospinal, synovial, intrapleural and the gastrointestinal system

sources.quote: Body fluids are found in two main areas of the body called intracellular and extracellular compartments.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Body Fluids

sources.quote: Intracellular fluids (ICF) are found inside cells and are made up of protein, water, electrolytes, and solutes.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Body Fluids

sources.quote: The most abundant electrolyte in intracellular fluid is potassium.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Body Fluids

sources.quote: In fact, intracellular fluid accounts for 60% of the volume of body fluids and 40% of a person’s total body weight!
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Body Fluids

sources.quote: Extracellular fluids (ECF) are fluids found outside of cells.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Body Fluids

sources.quote: The most abundant electrolyte in extracellular fluid is sodium.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Body Fluids

sources.quote: Extracellular fluids can be further broken down into various types.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Body Fluids

sources.quote: Intravascular fluid is whole blood volume and includes red blood cells, white blood cells, plasma, and platelets.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Body Fluids

sources.quote: Interstitial fluid refers to fluid outside of blood vessels and between the cells.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Body Fluids

sources.quote: The remaining extracellular fluid, also called transcellular fluid, refers to fluid in areas such as cerebrospinal, synovial, intrapleural, and the gastrointestinal system.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Body Fluids
